name: tui-snapper
tagline: btrfs snapshots, managed by snapper, from the terminal
description:
A terminal UI for the btrfs snapshots `snapper` manages. It lists every config and its history — pre/post pairs from package upgrades next to the hourly timeline snapshots — compares any two of them, and shows what changed file by file, with a read-only diff for anything you want to look at closely.

It creates, deletes, relabels and cleans up snapshots too, and puts individual files back with `undochange` without touching the rest of the filesystem. Every one of those is shown as the exact `snapper` command line and confirmed before it runs; starting the tool only reads.

Rollback is the one thing that genuinely differs between machines, so it is detected rather than assumed: where `snapper rollback` is the mechanism it is offered with a full warning, and on an Omarchy or limine-snapper-sync layout the boot menu entries are read from `/boot/limine.conf` and shown read-only, because that is where the rollback really happens.

`--demo` runs the whole UI against a sample history, so you can try it without a btrfs filesystem to risk.

screenshots.caption: The snapshot history: pre/post pairs, timeline snapshots and the pinned ones, newest first
What changed between two snapshots, created and deleted and modified paths together
One file's unified diff between the two snapshots, read-only and scrollable
The confirm dialog, showing the exact snapper command line before it runs
The rollback screen on a limine layout: the boot menu entries, read-only, and why
The help screen, generated from the action table

keys.action: Compare two snapshots; a post snapshot pairs with its own pre
Mark a snapshot: two marks are a range, many are one delete
Create a snapshot: description, type and cleanup algorithm
Delete the selected snapshot, or every marked one
Change a snapshot's description / cleanup algorithm
Run a cleanup: number, timeline or empty-pre-post
In the diff: put the selected files back with undochange
Rollback, or how this machine actually rolls back

notes.impact: snapper has no `--jsonout`, and both the config list and the snapshot list are read as JSON, so nothing can be listed at all
`snapper undochange` cannot recreate a path that sits directly under the subvolume root, so putting back a deleted top-level file or directory fails with "failed to create"
`snapper diff` is broken for LVM-based configs, so the file view comes back empty there even when the compare screen lists the change

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-snapper
cd tui-snapper && make demo
source.note: make demo needs no btrfs filesystem and no root.

pacman.note: Upgrades then arrive with the rest of your system updates.

apt.note: Upgrades then arrive with the rest of your system updates.

dnf.note: Upgrades then arrive with the rest of your system updates.

zypper.note: The rpm repository is shared with dnf; zypper support is not tested yet.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-snapper/releases/download/v{version}/tui-snapper_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-snapper
sudo install -m0755 tui-snapper /usr/local/bin/tui-snapper
binary.note: Static, no runtime dependencies beyond the snapper binary it drives.

security.needs_sudo: Reads too, not only writes: snapper opens its subvolumes directly, so even listing snapshots needs root. Run with sudo, or leave sudo = "sudo -n" configured. create, delete, modify, cleanup, undochange and rollback change things, and each is confirmed first. --demo escalates nothing.
